messages:
sylvie: Quick follow-up to the rollout-metadata divergence. Two landed PRs use different shapes: PR-compact emits a tiny 'fingerprint' string + flag bits; PR-full stores a self-describing JSON with source, cohort, fallback_order, expires_at, and provenance. We should agree on a single upgrade path before consumers rely on either.

marc: Can we paste minimal examples side-by-side? makes tradeoffs obvious.

(sylvie pasted) Compact example:
```json
{"fingerprint":"fp:9a3b...","bits":5}
```
Full example:
```json
{
  "source":"registry/v4",
  "cohort":"exp-2026-06-a",
  "fallback_order":["sm-v2","sm-v2-int8"],
  "expires_at":"2026-06-30T00:00:00Z",
  "provenance":[{"commit":"b33f","actor":"hana"}]
}
```

hana: My read: full JSON is best for CP records and audits; fingerprint is best when attached to millions of inference rows. We need a bridge pattern.

marc: Bridge = keep canonical full JSON in CP and issue a compact fingerprint for the hot path. Two questions: is fingerprint an opaque pointer (mutable) or content-based (immutable)?

sylvie: I'm advocating content-based fingerprint (sha256-like) mapping to an immutable canonical record. That gives auditability and easy dedupe. If semantics must change, create a new fingerprint and link the previous under "supersedes".

hana: How do we handle routing without blocking on CP? Dedicated/private runtimes can't hit CP per request. Proposal: CP returns both fingerprint and a small "snapshot_token" (routing hint) when a rollout is created. Runtime attaches fingerprint + snapshot_token to requests. Local runtime cache maps fingerprint -> canonical JSON. On cache miss, try CP fetch with short timeout (e.g., 25-40ms). If CP unreachable or timed out, fallback to interpreting snapshot_token for routing.

marc: Snapshot_token should be strictly bounded in size. Recommend <= 224 bytes and only include fields needed for routing: last_commit_short, cohort_short, primary_variant, routing_priority. Document the exact schema for snapshot_token so clients can parse it safely.

sylvie: Migration semantics: add two optional non-breaking fields to rollout envelopes: "fingerprint" (string) and "snapshot_token" (string/base64). Older services ignore them; newer services use fingerprint -> GET /fingerprints/{fingerprint}. CP stores canonical JSON under /fingerprints.

hana: Validation rules: canonical records are immutable. Mutations require issuing a new fingerprint; record the link via "prev_fingerprint" in canonical JSON. Also include a "lifecycle" enum: transient|standard|permanent for GC.

marc: Retention: transient 30d, standard 180d, permanent 10y. CP will run GC and provide an export endpoint so compliance can archive before deletion.

sylvie: Operational SLO: GET /fingerprints/{id} should be 50ms p95. Runtimes must not block longer than a configurable threshold; default fallback timeout 35ms.

hana: Rollout plan (feature-flagged):
1) Stage A: CP emits fingerprint in events only (no runtime emission).
2) Stage B: CP responds to create requests with fingerprint + snapshot_token; runtimes attach them to telemetry only.
3) Stage C: Runtimes enable snapshot-based routing and local caching; CP->runtime anchor fetch used on cache miss.

marc: Tests and checklist: backward compatibility tests (old services ignore fields), snapshot size enforcement, cache-miss latency benchmarks, uniqueness tests for identical canonical records deduped to same fingerprint, and GC/export validation.

sylvie: Action items: I'll draft the migration appendix with exact field names (fingerprint, snapshot_token) and snapshot schema budget. Hana, can you draft the runtime cache & timeout policy? Marc, ops checklist and export workflow? I'll PR the appendix tomorrow under the feature flag.

devops-bot: Note: schema changes require a documented migration plan, rollback playbook, and test plan. See /playbooks/schema-change-template.

sylvie: Thanks. One final naming ask: let's avoid using the old term "pin" in new fields to reduce ambiguity. If no objections by EOD I'll open the migration PR. :thumbsup:
